the selection-side read that composes it
the page's spelling of the exported call
the inherited-gate cases over the exported read

summary: `isPickableNow` takes the queue the entry sits in, and an entry is pickable only where every ancestor's gate would pass too
acceptance: a `work` entry under a parked, unsettled-`blockedBy` or unasserted-capability ancestor is unpickable through the exported read and through selection alike, and `isPickableNow` takes the queue rather than a blocker set its caller composed
tests: a work entry under a parked group is not pickable
a work entry under a group whose blockedBy has not settled is not pickable
a work entry under a group gated on an unasserted capability is not pickable
a work entry two groups below a parked root is not pickable
pins: a work entry under an open group stays pickable

interface.changes: `isPickableNow` takes the queue the entry sits in and answers over its ancestors' gates as well as its own; a caller no longer composes a settled-blocker set for it
interface.hides: which tags have settled, and that an ancestor's gate has to be walked at all
interface.rejected: a second exported read for the inherited case beside the flat one — two spellings of the switch is exactly how the tooling read and selection come to disagree about what pickable means

notes: `isPickableNow(entry, shippedTags, …)` reads the entry's own gate alone, so a `blockedBy` declared once on a goal holds nothing beneath it. Breaking on the package's public surface: the 0.22.0 cut's migration note walks the signature (`spec/cli.md`, *Versioning policy*), which is the cut's and not this entry's. Siblings on `src/selection.ts` and that page serialize against it.
